column1: # The level 0 swipe corpus (bead tla-7xql.2, epic tla-7xql).
# 80 items over the five templates in swipe/level0/TEMPLATES.tsv. Every claim
# is a CONSTANT-level TLA+ expression: no variable, no prime, no temporal
# operator. That is what lets this rung run with no model screen at all, which
# is the whole reason the epic picks level 0 first.
# Rows are tab-delimited and carry the literal marker ITEM in field 1, so prose
# in this file can never be read as data. Read rows with awk -F'\t' or cut,
# never with IFS=$'\t' read: tab is IFS whitespace, so a run of tabs collapses
# AN ITEM ROW. Eleven fields, in order:
#    3  template   T1-T5, resolving to a TEMPLATES.tsv row
#    4  ask        the tag shown WITH the question: holds or implies
#    5  kind       the item's own kind: true, false, vacuous or illformed
#    6  swipe      right, left or down. Derived from field 5 by the bake
#    7  rc_claim   the exit code of ASSUME (claim). Written by the bake
#    8  rc_wf      the exit code of ASSUME ((claim) \/ ~(claim)). Same
#    9  claim      the single line the reader sees
#   10  vacuity    a level 0 witness that the claim is vacuous, or -
#   11  correction the one line that gets it right, always present
# FIELDS 6, 7 AND 8 ARE OWNED BY swipe/level0/bake.sh. Do not hand-edit them.
# `bake.sh --write` measures them with TLC and writes them back, `bake.sh
# --check` confirms them, and harness/test-swipe-level0.sh gates the result.
# Fields 4, 5, 9, 10 and 11 are authored, and field 5 is the author's
# PREDICTION, which the bake is there to contradict.
# WHY FIELD 4 AND FIELD 5 ARE SEPARATE, which is a finding rather than a
# preference. Decision D5 on the epic says the item's kind is tagged in the
# question, and decision D3 says the kind is kept in the data so accuracy can
# be split by it. Those cannot be the same column: D3's kind IS the answer, so
# showing it with the question gives the item away. So field 4 is the tag the
# reader sees, naming which of the epic's question kinds this line is, and
# field 5 is the kind the data keeps. See swipe/README.md.
# FIELD 10 MAKES VACUITY A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A CLAIM. A vacuous item and
# a plainly true one both exit 0, so TLC alone cannot tell them apart. The
# witness is a second level 0 expression that holds exactly when the item is
# vacuous, and the bake runs it in the same batch, so the vacuous label has a
# NO ITEM MAY DEPEND ON \div WITH A NEGATIVE DIVIDEND, and that is a finding
# rather than a taste. The jar's own Naturals.tla states the contract:
#   a % b  and  a \div b  are defined so that for any integers  a  and  b
#   with  b > 0 , the following formula is true:
# TLC 2026.07.31.184830 breaks it. Measured with PrintT on 2026-10-17:
# remainder follows the contract and sits in 0..4, so it is the quotient that
# is wrong: it truncates toward zero where the contract forces it to round
# TLC is the authority the bake reads, so an item on -17 \div 5 would ship
# TLC's answer as the truth and teach a falsehood. Three authored items hit
# this and were replaced rather than re-labeled. harness/test-swipe-level0.sh
# carries a tripwire on the broken identity, so a TLC that fixes it turns the
# suite red and whoever reads this can lift the constraint.
# FIELD 11 IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IT IS NOT DECORATION. Measured on this task
# shape and recorded as L2 on the epic: a falsehood is reproduced later at .19
# with no feedback, .15 with a bare verdict, and .04 with the verdict plus the
# corrected claim. A bare verdict sits on the measured floor, so every row

column11: A power set has two members for every member of the original, so three gives eight.

Four things taken two at a time gives six pairs.
Both sides hold, so the implication holds.
Adding 3 to a set that already holds it changes nothing, and 3 is still a member.
A set holds each value once, so this one has three members.

A cross product multiplies the two sizes, so this one has fifteen pairs.
UNION flattens the family into one set, and that set has four members.

Cardinality is for finite sets, and Nat is not one, so the line has no value.
Asking whether 1 belongs to a power set asks what the members of 1 are, and a number has none.
Equality binds tighter than negation, so this reads as the negation of 1 = 2.
The exponent binds tighter than the product, so it is two times nine.
Addition binds tighter than the interval, so the upper bound is five.
